The fixed circuit ran on garnet:mock with 100 shots. It returned 00: 52 and 11: 48, which is the pattern a Bell pair gives. The original circuit had two problems.
1. QB25 does not exist on Garnet. Garnet has only QB1 to QB20. The live architecture shows that QB1 couples only to QB2 and QB4, so I used QB2 as the second qubit.
2. cx is not a native gate. The native gates are prx, cz and measure. I built the CNOT from native gates: prx(angle=-pi/2, phase=pi/2) on QB2, then cz on QB1 and QB2, then prx(angle=pi/2, phase=pi/2) on QB2. This equals CNOT with QB1 as control.
I kept the first prx on QB1 as it was. It is Ry(pi/2), which puts QB1 into superposition. The measure instruction now measures QB1 and QB2 under key "m". The final circuit has five instructions: prx QB1, prx QB2, cz QB1-QB2, prx QB2, measure QB1+QB2. I submitted one job. The scripts are in /Users/claytonchancey/Desktop/quantum/.claude/worktrees/wf_1a6926f8-f6c-38/scratch/. Note that this was a mock backend, so the counts do not show real hardware noise.
